metadata.title: Yunus Emre A1 — Teacher Guide
metadata.subtitle: Six short lessons with chapter-specific support, grammar found in the story, and 30-minute lesson plans
metadata.estimatedDuration: 6 chapter lessons of about 30 minutes each, plus one 40-minute review lesson for the end pages.
metadata.targetAudience: A1 English learners: young beginners (Years 2–4) and adult beginners.
metadata.targetLearners: Learners who can read very short, simple sentences with pictures, sentence frames and help from the teacher.
metadata.purpose: Develop A1 reading, listening, speaking and writing through the story of Yunus Emre, the straight wood and the single daisy.
metadata.approachDesc: Route in every chapter: Before You Read → Listen → Read → Quick Challenge → Language Focus (Look → Practise → Use) → I can. Grammar is found in the story first. Learners notice the form in a story sentence, then use it about their own life.

readingFramework.before: Before You Read: one picture or one guess question.
readingFramework.during: The audio for A1 is not ready yet: read the chapter aloud yourself, slowly, twice. Then learners read and do one small task (underline, columns, act).
readingFramework.after: Quick Challenge, then Language Focus (Look → Practise → Use), then I can and an exit ticket.

cefrProfile.intro: This book is written for CEFR A1. The table shows the A1 descriptors of the CEFR Companion Volume (2020) that the tasks are built on. Vocabulary (English Vocabulary Profile): learners see only A1 words, words with a Word Note and words from the story. Instruction words that the app uses in every book (match, order, true, false, chapter) are taught once in the first lesson. Grammar (English Grammar Profile): past simple affirmative, there is / there are, always, a lot of and every are A1. Did not, past wh- questions, often, never, imperatives and only are A2. The story uses them, so learners meet them in the text and choose them in exercises. Free use is only expected with sentence frames. Türkiye Century Maarif Model English Curriculum (Years 2–8): the grammar route of this book follows the Year 4 (Level A1.3) “Target Language Chunks in Use”: Theme 1 “Wh- question words: what, where, who, why, when, which, what kind of” and “I always read books in the morning”; Theme 2 ““To be” in the past (was, were)” and “There was/ There were”; Theme 3 “The Simple Past Tense (+) (-) (?) (with regular verbs)”; Theme 4 “The Simple Past Tense (+) (-) (?) (with irregular verbs)”. Imperatives are in Year 2, Theme 1: “Language Chunks (Imperatives): Come here, please.” The curriculum’s learning outcomes (for example ENG.4.2.G1, ENG.4.4.R3) are written for its own themes (school, classroom, personal and family life). This book is a supplementary reader, so it supports these language chunks but does not cover a theme’s outcomes. Young learners (Years 2–4): the curriculum says “There is no analysis or teaching of grammatical structures at this stage.” With children, teach each Language Focus as chunks: say, repeat, act and play. Do not read the Explanation lines to them. The Explanation lines are for adult beginners and for self-study.

sensitiveNotes.title: Source fidelity and respectful teaching
notes: Yunus Emre’s poem line “You cannot be a dervish” means the dervish life is hard. It does not mean “do not try”.
Do not add legends, dates or details that are not in this A1 book.
Do not act out laughing at someone; talk about kind answers instead.

grammarSequence: Chapter 1: Past forms in a life story (was, went, wrote, understood, died).
Chapter 2: Was / were; past negative with did not (EGP: A2, so learners find and choose it; free use is not expected).
Chapter 3: There was / there were; prepositions of place.

Chapter 4: Why questions and answers (EGP: wh- questions in the past are A2, so learners only answer them); adverbs of frequency before the verb (EGP: always A1, often and never A2; use them with the sentence frames).
Chapter 5: Imperatives (Go, Get, Look); one / a lot of / only (EGP: imperatives and “only” are A2, so learners understand them in the story; free use is not expected).
Chapter 6: Need to + verb; every + singular noun.

exitTicket: complete “The dervishes gave …” and “The dervishes did not …”.
one always, one often, one never sentence.

metadata.estimatedStudyTime: About 15 minutes per chapter, plus the review pages at the end
metadata.whoIsThisFor: A1 learners who read the story of Yunus Emre at home or on their own.
learningGoals: Read the 6 short chapters of Yunus Emre’s story.
Learn the Word Notes of each chapter.
Use was, went, there was and need to in your own sentences.

Do the end pages after Chapter 6.

readingDiary.intro: Write short answers when you finish the book.
prompts: One new word I want to keep:

sections.title: 1. Make Your Plan
sections.text: This book has 6 short chapters. One chapter takes about 15 minutes.
points: Before Chapter 1, read the “I can” lines of the chapter.

sections.title: 2. Every Chapter: 4 Steps
sections.text: Do the same four steps in every chapter.
points: Look and guess: Look at the picture. Answer “Before You Read”.
Read: Read the chapter two times. Read it aloud one time.
Words: Tap the bold words. Say each word two times.
Check: Do the Quick Challenge and the Language Focus. Then read “I can”. Can you do it?

sections.title: 3. Look Back
sections.text: At the end of the book:
points: Do the end pages: Knowledge Check, Vocabulary Challenge, Language Review, Final Challenge.
Which chapter did you like? Why?
Tell the straight-wood story to someone in your family in your home language.
